title: Dependent Products in the χ-Based ASASA Second Differential
summary: For χ-based ASASA’s second differential, independence predicts bias one sixteenth but disagrees with experiments; determine the products’ joint distribution under the constant-sum constraint.

formal_statement.body: In the $\chi$-based ASASA scheme, the second differential contains four bit-product terms whose four inputs sum to a constant. Modeling the four products as independent random binary variables, each zero with probability $3/4$, yields a simplified sum distribution with bias $2^{-4}$; experiments show that this independence model is inaccurate and introduces a significant discrepancy. The unresolved task is to characterize accurately the joint distribution of the four dependent products under the constant-sum constraint, so that the distributional analysis of the second differential is rigorously grounded.

scope.domain: Differential cryptanalysis of the χ-based ASASA construction.
assumptions: The four inputs to the bit-product terms sum to a constant.
parameters: Four bit-product terms — dependent binary variables in the second differential
Probability 3/4 — modeled chance that each product is zero under independence
Bias one sixteenth — simplified prediction for the sum under independence
scope.unresolved_remainder: Accurately characterize the joint distribution of the four dependent products under the constant-sum constraint and thereby rigorously ground the second-differential analysis.

progress.summary: The source reports that experiments expose a significant discrepancy in the independent-product approximation because the four inputs sum to a constant. It temporarily disregards this dependence and says it will return to the issue.
citation_labels: Brice Minaud et al., Key-Recovery Attacks on ASASA
